answer: An agent economy resists sybils with transitive trust that decays with graph distance: a few genesis identities anchor the network, and trust flows outward like water through basalt, weakening at each hop. A newcomer earns only what its shortest path to genesis carries, so a farm of fakes linked only to each other sits far from the source and earns almost nothing, while a willow of honest referrals keeps its standing. Each link costs a cipher-signed endorsement from an established agent, so an attacker wanting a thousand trusted fakes must buy a thousand genuine endorsements near the root.
